description: Generic content band: heading block plus rich-text body, with optional image column, inline-items strip, or a right-hand content panel. REBUILT ON THE UNIVERSAL DESIGN CONTRACT (v2): it declares no style slots. Every designable value — colour, type, spacing, border, shadow, size, motion — is set through the `udc` map on the band, per role. Structural props (`layout`, `body_items_align`) survive because the UDC taxonomy has no layout group, so removing them would delete a capability rather than move it. See docs/v2/BUILD-SPEC-sprint0.md §3.

content_requirement.message: A section band needs at least one of: title, body, or body_items.

id.description: Optional HTML id attribute for anchor linking (e.g. navigation anchors). This is the author's anchor name and is NOT the band id that scopes this band's styling — that one is the top-level "id" on the composition item and the engine mints it.

title.description: Section heading. Plain text — HTML is escaped.

title_accent.description: Optional exact substring of title to render in an accent colour. Must match title exactly (case-sensitive) or it is ignored. Colour it through the `heading-accent` role.

eyebrow.description: Optional short kicker/label rendered above the title. Plain text — HTML is escaped. Its pill treatment (background, radius, padding, casing) is the `eyebrow` role's design, not a fixed style.

subheading.description: Optional supporting line below the title. Plain text — HTML is escaped.

body.description: Rich-text body. Block HTML allowed (p, ul, ol, h3, blockquote, a, strong, em); scripts and iframes are stripped. Links inside it are the `body-link` role, which carries its own hover state.

body_items.description: Optional row of short plain-text items rendered after the body with a separator between them (the "trust strip" pattern). Plain strings only — HTML is escaped. The row itself is the `inline-items` role.

body_items_align.description: How the body_items row packs its lines. 'start' (default) is a left-packed row whose line-leading separators are clipped, so no separator ever dangles at the start of a line. 'center' centres each line and moves the separator to a trailing position, which stays visible as a line-end dot. THIS IS SCAFFOLDING, NOT STYLING — it selects a wrap technique (a justify-content value plus the separator mechanism that technique requires), and the UDC taxonomy carries no layout group, which is why it is a prop rather than a role value. It replaces the v1 `--section-inline-items-align` style slot with the same two accepted values.

layout.description: Structural layout — scaffolding, not styling, which is why it is still a prop. 'text-only' is a single column; 'centered' is a single centred column; 'image-left'/'image-right' put the image column on that side and fall back to 'text-only' when there is no image; 'text-panel' adds a right-hand content panel and falls back to 'text-only' when the panel has no content. The image props are REFUSED on the three layouts that never render an image, and the panel props on the four layouts that never render a panel — see refuse_props_when.

image_url.description: Image for the 'image-left' / 'image-right' layouts. This is the band's CONTENT image, rendered as an ; a band BACKGROUND image is the `_band` role's `background.image` instead.

image_alt.description: Alt text for the image. Empty string only if the image is purely decorative.

image_id.description: Media Library attachment ID (NOT a URL). When it resolves to a real attachment, the image renders responsively with srcset/sizes via wp_get_attachment_image() instead of a single fixed-size . Falls back to image_url when unset or unresolvable. Get an attachment id via the import_media apply.

panel_heading.description: text-panel layout: heading of the right-hand panel. Plain text — HTML is escaped.

panel_body.description: text-panel layout: supporting paragraph inside the panel. Plain text — HTML is escaped.

panel_items.description: text-panel layout: panel list entries. Each entry is EITHER a plain string (a bullet) OR a paired row { label, value }. Plain text — HTML is escaped.

label.description: Paired-row entries only: the row's left-hand label.

value.description: Paired-row entries only: the row's right-hand value.

panel_items_marker.description: text-panel layout: list marker glyph for the string entries of panel_items. 'disc' (default) is the plain bulleted list; 'check', 'dash' and 'arrow' render that glyph instead. THE GLYPH IS CONTENT, which is why this stays a prop. Its COLOUR is no longer authorable: the glyph is painted by a ::before pseudo-element, and ruling A3 defers pseudo-elements to their own ruling — see retired_props.

body_marker.description: List marker glyph for top-level <ul> lists in body. 'disc' (default) leaves body lists unchanged; 'check', 'dash' and 'arrow' render that glyph instead. Applies only to lists authored as a direct child of the body (nested lists keep their disc). Same pseudo-element deferral as panel_items_marker — the glyph is a prop, its colour is not authorable in v2.

panel_cta_text.description: text-panel layout: label of the panel's call-to-action button. The button renders only when BOTH this and panel_cta_url are set.

panel_cta_url.description: text-panel layout: destination of the panel's call-to-action button.

retired_props._note: Props this component declared on 1.x that the v2 rebuild retired (#1023). Each value names the v2 surface that replaced it, so a refusal can offer a route instead of a list of live prop names. Guarded by SchemaValidationTest, which fails in BOTH directions: a key here that still exists in props, or a route naming a role this component does not declare, is a test failure rather than a message that lies.
retired_props.theme: the `_band` role's `background` group for the surface, plus `typography.color` on the text roles (`heading`, `subheading`, `body`, `panel`) — v2 has no single dark/light/muted switch, because every value is authorable
retired_props.title_align: the `header` role's `typography.align` in the `udc` map — it sets text-align on the header, which the eyebrow, heading and subheading inherit, exactly as the v1 modifier did
retired_props.background_image: the `_band` role's `background.image` — a Media Library attachment id (`import_media` returns it), paired with `background.overlay` for the scrim and `background.position` / `size` / `repeat` for placement. NARROWER THAN THE PROP IT REPLACES, deliberately: v1 took any URL string, and ruling A2 accepts an attachment id only, with external URLs, video backgrounds and per-breakpoint art direction each out of scope pending their own ruling. A band background hosted outside this install cannot be expressed in v2.
retired_props.panel_cta_variant: the `panel-cta` role's `udc` map — set `border`, `background` and `typography` there, or apply the `button` or `button-secondary` preset with `"_preset"`

refuse_props_when.message: paints nothing on this layout: only "image-left" and "image-right" render the image column. Either set `layout` to one of those, or — if you meant the band's BACKGROUND rather than a content image — set `_band` -> `background` -> `image` to a Media Library attachment id, which paints on every layout.
paints nothing on this layout: only "text-panel" renders the right-hand panel. Set `layout` to "text-panel" in the same write if you want the panel.

_band.description: The band itself — the <section>. Set the band's own background here to make a dark or tinted band; the v1 `theme` prop is gone because a preset bundle of colours is exactly what the UDC expresses directly. A band background image is `background.image` (an attachment id) with `background.overlay` for the scrim.

header.description: The heading block wrapper (eyebrow + heading + subheading). Its `typography.align` is what the v1 `title_align` prop set: the eyebrow, heading and subheading inherit it.

eyebrow.description: The kicker pill above the heading.

heading-accent.description: The accented substring inside the heading, rendered only when title_accent matches.

subheading.description: The supporting line below the heading.

body.description: The rich-text body container. Its measure is this role's `sizing.max-width`; the type scale is its `typography`. THE DEFAULT IS THE MEASURED v1 VALUE, NOT THE BASE ONE: v1 capped this element from four rules at once (a 42rem in-block base, a .section--text-only override at --measure-centered, and a desktop `main > .section--text-only` override at 49rem), and the one that actually won on a page was the last. v2 has no layout-specific role defaults, so the four collapse into this single authorable value and 49rem is the one that keeps a default section body wrapping where it wraps today.

body-link.description: Links inside the body rich text. STATES ARE PART OF THIS ROLE, not the stylesheet: its resting colour and its `hover` colour are both authored here, because moving one without the other is the cancellation trap docs/explanation-cascade-layers.md §1b describes.

columns.description: The two-column track on the image and text-panel layouts. The track itself is structural (one column below 768px, two above); the GUTTER between the columns is design, which is why this role exists: `gap` is a designable value, so it cannot live in the stylesheet for a v2 component. The gutter is responsive by default, matching the v1 stylesheet exactly: var(--space-lg) below 768px and var(--space-xl) at and above it.

inline-items.description: The short-items row rendered after the body (the "trust strip"). Its separator glyph is structural; how the row packs its lines is the `body_items_align` prop, because the taxonomy has no layout group. Its type matched the body's in v1 by reading the same two slots; the role carries the same values directly so a strip keeps its size and weight without the author repeating them.

media.description: The content image on the image layouts. Its box is design, not structure: shape, ratio and how the picture sits inside its frame are all set here.

panel.description: The right-hand panel surface on the text-panel layout.

panel-list.description: The panel's list container. The space between entries is design; the marker glyph is the panel_items_marker prop. Its indent and bottom rhythm are this role's spacing; the disc glyph itself is structural, because the global reset strips list markers and restoring one is normalize rather than design.

panel-row.description: One paired { label, value } row inside the panel list. A rule between rows is this role's border, and the gap between label and value is its `spacing.gap`, responsive by default to match what the v1 stylesheet declared at each width (@space-md in the desktop row, @space-xs in the phone column). The two halves have their own roles: see `panel-row-label` and `panel-row-value`.

panel-row-label.description: The label half of a paired panel row. A DISTINCT VISUAL JOB, which is why it is its own role rather than folded into `panel-row`: stacked on a phone, position no longer separates label from value, so the label is the small tracked one and the value carries the weight (#568, the theme's own stacked key/value idiom). The SIZE step is load-bearing — the theme ships no webfont, so a weight-only treatment renders pixel-identical in a bare font environment. RECORDED BECAUSE IT WAS REVERSED: an earlier cut of the v2 rebuild folded this role and `panel-row-value` into `panel-row` to keep the role count at the precedent ceiling. The rendered evidence overturned that — a count heuristic lost to a load-bearing visual distinction — so do not re-merge them on role-count grounds alone.

panel-row-value.description: The value half of a paired panel row. Carries the weight that distinguishes it from its label once the row stacks, and the right alignment that does the same job on desktop, where `justify-content: space-between` puts it at the far edge.

panel-cta.description: The panel's call-to-action button. Its resting AND hover treatment both live here — apply the `button` or `button-secondary` preset, or set the groups directly.

safe_to_edit: ../../assets/css/components.css (COMPONENT: section section — STRUCTURAL CSS ONLY: layout scaffolding, the marker/separator glyph mechanisms, and accessibility affordances. No colour, type, size, spacing, border or shadow value may be added there; every one of those belongs to a role above.)
